summary:
Submitted a final small product that closes the last unread boundary in the target profile.

Context from the index: three findings are confirmed_in_scope, the restart check is accepted as a bounded negative, the heartbeat-handler exploration is recorded with its observed difference, map v12 is the accepted basis, audit units are exhausted, and pending_work is empty.

Product contents (draft-relative submission.json with the updated map.json and one newly acquired source range SR-COMPAT-GOMOD = raft-compat/go.mod 1-20):

Reading the compatibility directory shows it is its own Go module whose go.mod replaces github.com/hashicorp/raft with this working copy and requires a previous release plus an older tag, driving mixed-version clusters through a shared test cluster helper for rolling upgrades and pre-vote behaviour. It is therefore recorded as a new infrastructure surface rather than a protocol responsibility, and the target profile's list of unread boundaries is now empty. No behavior, fact, edge or confirmed finding is affected.

The feedback (ref_ids target_profile) records the answered boundary and carries the surviving frontier: the non-atomic (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair, the election-restriction chain, the FSM consistency question, the pre-vote and TimeoutNow liveness residuals, the recovered-index fencing question, the possible transport cost of the unanswered shutdown heartbeat, and the two out-of-snapshot questions. Unit admission exhaustion is stated so these remain named premises rather than new obligations.

Preflight `validate` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. Acceptance and the final map version remain with the controller.
